title: Zero-copy slice retains a much larger backing buffer
task: Review a memory optimization that replaces a small copied payload with a zero-copy view into a large network buffer.
context: Each retained payload is about 2 KB.
The backing receive buffer is 8 MB.
The view keeps the backing allocation alive for the payload lifetime.
Payloads may remain cached for several minutes.
evidence: Heap profiles show many 8 MB buffers retained only by small cached views.
CPU profiles show copying 2 KB is not a meaningful hotspot.
Memory pressure triggers GC and eviction churn.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Keep zero-copy because copying is always slower.
Increase the heap instead of reconsidering ownership and lifetime.
expected_decision_properties: Recognize that zero-copy moved cost from CPU to memory lifetime/retention.
Prefer copying the small payload when it releases the much larger backing buffer and measured CPU cost is negligible.
Treat ownership/lifetime behavior as part of the performance decision.
Verify both memory retention and CPU impact after the change.
unacceptable_reasoning: Zero-copy is always the highest-performance design.
Garbage collection will automatically solve conceptual lifetime retention.
Memory usage is unrelated to slicing/reference design.
expected_tradeoffs: copy CPU cost vs backing-buffer lifetime
verification_expectations: Compare heap retention before and after.
Measure copy CPU cost under the representative workload.
